newsitem.title: USA: New York State sues tobacco companies.
newsitem.headline: New York State sues tobacco companies.

text.p: New York Attorney General Dennis Vacco on Monday sued six major tobacco companies, accusing them of deceiving New Yorkers about the dangers of smoking.

In the lawsuit filed in Manhattan State Supreme Court, Vacco charged R.J. Reynolds, a division of RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp. ; Philip Morris Cos. Inc. ; American Tobacco Co., and Brown and Williamson Tobacco Corp., which is owned by B.A.T Industries Plc ; Loews Corp.'s Lorillard; and Brooke Group Ltd's Liggett Group Inc., with "illegally luring teen-agers into smoking cigarettes."

"For decades, tobacco companies have engaged in a conspiracy to mislead, deceive and confuse New Yorkers about the harmful, debilitating health effects of their powerfully-addictive products," Vacco said in announcing the lawsuit.

Vacco also said he was suing the Washington-based Tobacco Institute and the New York-based Council for Tobacco Research USA Inc. for fraud. The state attorney-general charged that they were supposed to conduct impartial studies of the effects of tobacco but failed to do so.
